blocker_detail: A manual TP=2 no-MTP launch on Spark3/Spark2 with DS4_VLLM_ENABLE_GB10_FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MOE=1 selected FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8 on both ranks, then failed during startup profiling in flashinfer/data/csrc/trtllm_batched_gemm_runner.cu:286: Error occurred when running GEMM, kernel bmm_MxE4m3_MxE2m1MxE4m3_Fp32_Ab32_Bb32_Cb32_t128x128x256u2_s4_et128x32_m256x128x32_c2x1x1_rM_TN_transOut_schPd2x1x2x3_biasFp32M_bN_tma_ldgstsSf_rgTma_clmp_swiGlu_lbW8_lsfbW4_dynB_sm100f. The Spark5/Spark6 alternate pair was also blocked because Spark6 had an existing ./ds4-eval process using about 103 GiB GPU memory; it was not killed without explicit user approval.
interpretation: The opt-in GB10 support gate is not a valid speed path yet. It proves vLLM can be forced to choose the FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4/MXFP8 backend on GB10, but the installed FlashInfer 0.6.11 TRTLLM SM100 routed-MoE GEMM fails at runtime on GB10/SM121 before API readiness.
required_next_command: Do not claim throughput from the GB10 FlashInfer patch. Either keep the production vLLM lane on the measured no-MTP backend, or test a FlashInfer/vLLM build with real SM121 TRTLLM MXFP4 support and rerun the same TP=2 c64/c128/c512 fanout.
support_probe_command: docker run --rm --gpus all -v /tmp/patch_vllm_ds4_gb10_flashinfer_moe.py:/tmp/patch.py:ro --entrypoint bash vllm-node-dsv4 -lc 'python3 /tmp/patch.py /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm --write && DS4_VLLM_ENABLE_GB10_FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MOE=1 python3 -c ...'
